text:
sam: Quick follow-up to the kernel-selection RFC — I prototyped a capability-gated path chooser to handle A100 / H100 / L4 differences. Wanted to share findings and get alignment on the rollout plan.

julia: Nice. High level summary first?

sam: TL;DR: keep a small set of specialized kernel paths (fp8-tc, fp16-tc, int8-inference, generic-cuda), detect GPU features at runtime into a compact capability mask, and pick the highest-priority compiled kernel for that mask. Fallbacks to generic kernels if specialized ones are missing. This avoids recompiling per-request and lets us A/B / toggle per-cluster.

omar: Which features are we using for the mask? tensorcore fp8, tensorcore fp16/bf16, structured sparsity, extended shmem, dp4a-style int ops?

sam: Prototype mask fields: [TENSORCORE_FP8, TENSORCORE_FP16_BF16, SPARSITY_ACCEL, INT8_DOT, SHARED_MEM_LARGE, WARP_MMA_EXT]. We keep it extensible. We map GPUs to masks during node init.

li: Any runtime cost for evaluating the mask? I assume we do it once on node startup.

sam: Exactly. We detect once during runtime init and populate a node-local kernel table. Kernel selection per-request then is just a small bitmask lookup + strcmp on model-profile key — constant time.

dena: How does this interact with JIT kernels / nvrtc / cuFFT-like compile steps? We don't want head-of-line stalls under load if we hit a new path.

sam: Good point. Strategy: pre-warm the kernel cache at deployment time for the common model variants and the GPU masks we expect in the fleet. Two mechanisms: 1) offline bake step (CI/packaging) that builds kernels for known masks; 2) background async JIT on node if an unexpected mask appears, with request throttling and immediate fallback to generic kernel until compiled.

julia: For H100, the ideal path is fp8 tensorcore + sparsity if model and accuracy allow, right? Any numbers from your perf runs?

sam: Yes. On our perf harness: for a 2K sequence LLM decode loop, fp8-tc+sparsity on H100 vs generic fp16 on A100 gave ~2.7x throughput improvement and ~46% lower token-flop cost for that model. L4 int8 path is ~1.8x vs generic on our trimmed-perfbert-like model with 1/4 power envelope. These are workload dependent but the ordering held across several tests.

omar: Are we gating fp8 use behind an explicit model opt-in? We should avoid silent precision changes that could cause quality regressions for users.

sam: We require an explicit model artifact flag (model.manifest.optimizations includes fp8_allowed, sparsity_allowed). Runtime will refuse fp8 kernels for a model that hasn't opted in. Also we keep eval regressions tied to rollout: if a model opts in, CI runs eval suites comparing fp16 vs fp8 quantization on tracked prompt sets.

li: Interface boundaries — where does kernel_selector live? SDK side or serving runtime?

sam: Kernel selector lives in the serving runtime (C++). The contract with higher layers is small: given model-config + request meta, return a kernel_variant_id. Model-config includes the optimization flags, target sequence length hint, and quantization profile. This keeps SDKs and control plane out of kernel logic but allows config overrides via the console.

dena: How do we express the fallback order? Data-driven or code-level?

sam: Data-driven. Each model version package ships a prioritized list like: [fp8-tc-sparse, fp8-tc, fp16-tc, int8-native, generic-cuda]. The node then intersects with GPU capability set and available compiled kernels. The first match is used. Admins can pin or disable entries via feature flags.

julia: What about memory layout differences for H100 fp8 kernels (packed formats)? Do we need model graph-transform steps?

sam: Yes, some kernels expect packed weights or special packing for MMA ops. Bake step handles repacking into the model package for the targeted kernel variants. We support on-the-fly repacking in a background thread for unbaked combos but prefer prebaked artifacts for predictable perf.

omar: Observability — how do we capture which path was used per-request?

sam: Add route-level telemetry: kernel_variant_id, gpu_mask, compile_hit (prebaked|jit|fallback), and latency/token counts. We'll surface stats in the Console and ship to Sentry/Prometheus. Alerts on quality regressions (eval metrics) and perf regressions (p95 latency increase > 10% for 1h).

li: Testing matrix sounds large: models x gpu masks x seq lengths. Practical approach?

sam: Start with a pivot set: 6 models (2 chat, 2 encoder, 2 small conv-ish), 3 seq lengths (512/2k/8k), and 3 GPU types (A100/H100/L4). That's 54 combos. We run perf + accuracy smoke tests on CI for any kernel change. For releases, run expanded perf farm.

dena: Rollout plan?

sam: Canary stages: 1) internal perf lab on dedicated H100/A100/L4 nodes (bake + run synthetic load), 2) 1% of dedicated cluster traffic with telemetry gating (~48h), 3) 10% with auto rollback triggers, 4) full. Also provide an org-level kill-switch in Console to disable specific kernel_variant_ids.

julia: Is there an escape hatch for very latency-sensitive customers who prefer A100-like deterministic paths?

sam: Yes — model config supports "force_variant": "fp16-tc" or "generic-cuda". For Dedicated nodes we can also set cluster-level enforced_variant via admin policy.

omar: Any security concerns with JIT compiling kernels from package artifacts? Code injection risk?

sam: We treat kernels as first-class artifacts and sign them. JIT sources are only accepted from trusted artifact repositories; node enforces signature checks. Also sandbox the JIT worker.

dena: One last operational question: what about multi-GPU scheduling when different GPUs in the same job have different masks?

sam: We prefer homogeneous allocations for GPU-bound inference. When heterogenous GPUs are unavoidable (rare for Dedicated), the scheduler pins a model shard to the subset of GPUs that satisfy the required mask, or falls back to the lowest-common-denominator variant. We avoid per-token migration across GPU types.

julia: Looks solid. Next steps?

sam: I'll open a short RFC addendum with the mask schema, kernel table format, and prewarm CI changes. Action items:
- sam: draft addendum and bake scripts (by EOD Friday)
- julia: add eval cases for fp8 smoke tests (next sprint)
- omar: run perf runbook on H100/L4 farm and share numbers (next week)
- li: add telemetry fields + Console UI stub (this week)

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: "kernel-bake-staging" -> started on nodes: h100-staging-03, a100-staging-01, l4-staging-02

sam: Thanks — will post the addendum link here once it's landed. :thumbsup:
